title: Demo scene
script:
A small coffee shop near the university, worn soft by years. Late-autumn light comes gold through a tall window beaded with rain. Hard rock murmurs from a speaker in the corner. The place has never been much — but it keeps its two constants: loud guitars and bad coffee.

At the corner table she always takes, a young woman sits reading, elbows planted on the wood. Wire-rimmed glasses — the kind that look a little like orthodontia — slip down her nose; her thin hands hold a dog-eared paperback. Her coffee has long gone cold, and the ashtray at her elbow is brimming.

A young man comes in from the rain and shakes the water from his coat. He knows the room, and he knows the table. He crosses to her and takes the chair across from her.

She looks up and gives a small, unhurried smile. Without a word she slides a paperback across the table toward him; he slides another one back. The everyday trade.

They fall into talk. The light slides from gold to bronze along the tabletop, and the rain thickens on the glass, blurring the street into soft smears of warm light.

She sets her book face-down, rests her chin on her thin hands, and watches him talk. He watches the rain. Neither of them says the thing. The afternoon just holds them there — two students, one worn table, a stack of paperbacks between them, and the last warm hour before the cold sets in.
